newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutscher Investment Trust funds grow in H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Deutscher Investment Trust funds grow in H1 1997.

text.p: Deutscher Investment Trust (DIT), the asset management arm of Germany's Dresdner Bank AG said on Friday 9.4 billion marks ($5.4 billion) in new cash volumes flowed into its investment funds in the first half of 1997.
In the same period, the group's total assets rose 17.4 percent to 128.4 billion marks. DIT's public funds grew at an above average pace, up by 10 billion marks to almost 60 billion marks.
Investor interest centred on equity funds, which showed a return of $2.8 billion in the first six months of the year, DIT said in a statement.
It said this was a sign of gowing interest in equity funds as an investment instrument in Germany.
-- Kate Kelland, Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525 ($ = 1.751 German Marks)
